name: Andorra
summary: Andorra is an EU Annex I listed territory (pets from it enter the EU without titer test or point-of-entry check). No dedicated official import page was found; in practice pets arrive via Spain or France, so that country's EU entry rules apply (microchip, rabies vaccination, EU pet passport or EU health certificate; titer test from unlisted countries).
microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid. (as required by the EU country of arrival)
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
rabies_titer: Per EU rules of the arrival country: required only from unlisted third countries.
parasite_treatment: None identified (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO, Northern Ireland).
documents: EU pet passport (from EU) or EU animal health certificate + non-commercial declaration (from third countries), as required by the EU arrival country.
quarantine: None identified if EU requirements are met.
timeline: As for the EU arrival country: at least 4 weeks from EU/listed origin; 4+ months from unlisted origin.
restricted_breeds: Not verified.
private_aviation: No airport in Andorra; private jets land in Spain (e.g. Andorra-La Seu d'Urgell, Barcelona) or France (e.g. Toulouse); EU entry rules and points of entry of that country apply for third-country arrivals.
export: Leaving: EU treats this territory as Annex I listed (pet passport/certificate, no titer, no point-of-entry requirement). Local export procedure not verified.
authority: Government of Andorra - Ministry of Agriculture (veterinary service); not verified

name: Austria
summary: EU rules (Reg. (EU) 2026/131): from EU/EEA/Switzerland, a microchipped pet with valid rabies vaccination and EU pet passport; from a third country, an EU animal health certificate (plus rabies titer test if the country is unlisted) and entry via a travellers' point of entry.
microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip, implanted or read before the rabies vaccination (a clearly readable tattoo applied before 3 July 2011 is still accepted). Microchips implanted under Reg. 576/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid.
vaccinations: Rabies: given by an authorised vet when the pet is at least 12 weeks old, on or after the microchip date; primary vaccination becomes valid 21 days after the primary protocol is completed; boosters given within the validity of the previous vaccination need no new waiting period.
rabies_titer: Not required from EU/EEA states, Switzerland, Northern Ireland or listed territories/third countries (Annex I: AD, CH, FO, GI, GL, IS, LI, MC, SM, VA; Annex II includes GB, JE, GG, IM, US, CA, AU, NZ, JP, AE, SG, HK, ME, RS and others; Reg. (EU) 2026/636 as amended by 2026/1228). From unlisted countries: blood sample taken by an authorised vet at least 30 days after rabies vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml at an EU-designated laboratory, sample taken no less than 90 days (3 months) before the animal health certificate is issued; copy of lab report must accompany the certificate. No retest needed if rabies vaccination is kept valid. The 3-month wait does not apply to EU-resident pets re-entering whose passport records a favourable test done before leaving the EU.
parasite_treatment: None required for entry (EU tapeworm rule applies only to FI, IE, MT, NO and Northern Ireland).
documents: From another EU/EEA state, Switzerland or Annex I territory: EU pet passport (new model, Reg. (EU) 2026/705; passports issued under Reg. 577/2013 before 22 Apr 2026 remain valid transitionally).

From a third country: EU animal health certificate (model Annex III, Reg. (EU) 2026/705) completed by an official/authorised vet and endorsed by the exporting country's competent authority. Valid 10 days from issue until the entry checks; then valid for onward travel in the EU for 6 months from the entry checks or until rabies vaccination expires, whichever is earlier. Certificates on the old Reg. 577/2013 model are accepted only if issued before 1 Oct 2026.
Owner's written declaration that the movement is non-commercial (Annex V Part 2, Reg. 2026/705).

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.
Young animals: this country does NOT accept unvaccinated/insufficiently vaccinated young pets (under ~15 weeks) from other EU states; never allowed from third countries.
quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.

Airport points of entry on the list published via the European Commission (dated 2006): Vienna, Linz, Klagenfurt, Salzburg, Graz, Innsbruck. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.

name: Switzerland
summary: EU-equivalent rules: from EU, microchip + valid rabies vaccination + pet passport; from third countries, health certificate (or Swiss/EU passport if already compliant), presentation at the red customs exit, and for rabies high-risk countries a titer test, minimum age 7 months and an FSVO import authorisation for direct flights.
microchip: Microchip required, implanted before rabies vaccination.
vaccinations: Rabies: first dose from 12 weeks of age, valid 21 days later; must follow microchipping.
rabies_titer: Required from rabies high-risk third countries: antibody titration test at an EU-designated laboratory with long waiting periods (EU standard: sample >=30 days after vaccination, travel >=3 months after sample). Animals under 7 months may not enter from high-risk countries. Not required from EU or listed/low-risk countries.
documents: From EU: Swiss or EU pet passport.
From third countries: Swiss/EU passport if already compliant, otherwise health certificate issued by exporting country's authorities.
From high-risk countries by direct flight: FSVO import authorisation (application form on blv.admin.ch).
Owner travelling separately: authorised person, owner within 5 days, written declaration in passport.
Max 5 pets per private vehicle unless for events (registered, >6 months old; third-country animals need FSVO authorisation).
import_permit: FSVO import authorisation required for direct air arrivals from rabies high-risk countries; otherwise none.
quarantine: None if requirements met; pets with missing documents are refused entry.
timeline: EU/low-risk origin: at least 4 weeks (microchip -> rabies vaccination at >=12 weeks -> 21 days). High-risk origin: at least 4 months and pet >=7 months old (vaccination -> titer test -> waiting period -> FSVO authorisation -> certificate).
restricted_breeds: Import of dogs with docked ears and/or tails is prohibited. Cantonal dog-breed rules exist but were not reviewed - check the destination canton.
private_aviation: From third countries, accompanied pets (cabin or excess baggage) may only fly into Basel, Geneva or Zurich; unaccompanied pets (air waybill) only Geneva or Zurich. Pets must be presented at the red customs exit for an entry control. Arrivals from EU/Schengen: no border vet check but documents required.
export: Destination rules apply; veterinary certificates for leaving are issued by the responsible cantonal veterinary service. Ensure Swiss re-entry conditions are met before departure.
authority: Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office (FSVO/BLV)

microchip: Required for routes via GB/EU per GB/EU rules; not required for GB-IoM movement.
vaccinations: Rabies: required for pets coming from the EU/other countries via GB under GB rules; not for GB-IoM movement.
rabies_titer: Only as required by GB rules for unlisted countries (pets must clear GB first).

documents: GB/NI to IoM: none.
From Ireland direct: pre-notify DEFA.
EU via GB: GB entry documents (pet passport/AHC) and DEFRA-authorised pet transporter by prior arrangement with DEFA.
import_permit: Direct import from non-EU countries prohibited.
quarantine: None for compliant GB-cleared pets.

name: Iceland
summary: Strict national regime (not the EU pet passport system): import permit from MAST, origin from an approved country, rabies vaccination plus titer test, multiple vaccinations/tests/parasite treatments, arrival only via Keflavík and minimum 14-day quarantine at an approved station.
microchip: ISO-compliant microchip; number verified at every veterinary procedure for import.
vaccinations: Rabies: valid vaccination; per MAST overview given at least 45-60 days before import (titer sample at earliest 30 days after vaccination).
Dogs: leptospirosis, distemper, infectious canine hepatitis, parvovirus, parainfluenza - last dose at least 14 days before import.
Cats: feline panleukopenia, rhinotracheitis, calicivirus - last dose at least 14 days before import.
Dogs from category 2 countries USA, Canada or Singapore: canine influenza vaccination also required (per certificate form).
rabies_titer: Required from all origins: sample at least 30 days after vaccination, result at least 0.5 IU/ml, EU-approved laboratory; valid while vaccination is kept up to date. For category 2 countries (e.g. Hungary, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Greenland, USA, Canada) travel only 90 days or more after sampling; animals qualify at earliest ~7 months old (category 1: ~4.5 months).
parasite_treatment: Internal + external parasite treatment twice: 21-28 days and 5-10 days before import (products registered for roundworm, tapeworm, lice, fleas, ticks). Dogs: Angiostrongylus vasorum test within 30 days OR preventive imidacloprid+moxidectin treatment 5-10 days before.
documents: MAST import permit (apply at least 30 days before; valid 1 year; fee payable).
MAST certificate of health and origin (D1/D2 dogs, C1/C2 cats by country category), completed by authorised vet 5-10 days before import after health exam.
Lab reports: rabies titer; dogs Brucella canis (within 30 days) and Leishmania (intact dogs, within 30 days); cats FeLV and FIV (within 30 days).
Scanned certificate + lab results to petimport@mast.is no later than 5 days before arrival (later submission may be rejected).
Originals travel with the animal; customs declaration (VAT if owned < 12 months).
import_permit: Yes - MAST import permit required before import. Animal must have lived in an approved category 1 or 2 country since birth or for the last 6 months. Category 1 includes all EU states except HU, PL, RO, SK (category 2), plus NO (excl. Svalbard), CH, LI, FO, GB, AU, JP, SG, AE.
quarantine: Minimum 14 days at an approved quarantine station (Reykjanesbær/Hafnir or Mósel/Hella), booked in advance; admissions only in set 3-day windows about 3 weeks apart; arrival at Keflavík 06:00-17:00 on admission dates; no overnight stays at the airport. Service dogs may apply for home quarantine.
timeline: Plan at least 4-6 months (category 2: ~7 months minimum age): import permit application (>=30 days before) -> book quarantine slot -> rabies vaccination -> titer test >=30 days later -> other vaccinations -> tests within 30 days of arrival -> parasite treatments at 21-28 and 5-10 days -> health exam + certificate 5-10 days before -> send to MAST >=5 days before -> fly to Keflavík on admission date.
restricted_breeds: Banned: wolf hybrids (10 generations); Pit Bull Terrier/Staffordshire Bull Terrier (service-dog form also lists American Staffordshire Terrier and American Bulldog), Fila Brasileiro, Tosa Inu, Dogo Argentino, Cane Corso, Presa Canario, Boerboel and crosses (5 generations), plus dogs MAST assesses as comparable. Pregnant/lactating animals not accepted.
private_aviation: Pets may only arrive by air at Keflavík Airport (only approved entry port; ferry arrival not permitted). Animals must be in a hard IATA-compliant crate (soft carriers not allowed); flight number and arrival time are recorded on the certificate; arrival must match a quarantine admission date and 06:00-17:00 window. Confirm with MAST and the quarantine station before planning a private-jet arrival.
export: Leaving Iceland: destination-country rules apply (EU treats Iceland as an Annex I listed territory - EU pet passport/certificate, no titer). Contact MAST for export certification.
authority: Icelandic Food and Veterinary Authority (MAST)

Non-commercial = max 5 dogs/cats/ferrets per movement (more only for competitions/shows/sporting events with written registration proof and animals over 6 months old). Pet must travel with owner or an authorised person within 5 days of the owner's journey (written declaration). Otherwise commercial rules (Reg. 2020/688 / TRACES) apply.

Young animals: this country authorises non-commercial entry from other EU states of pets under 12 weeks unvaccinated, or 12-16 weeks vaccinated but before the 21-day wait ends, with owner's declaration of no contact with rabies-susceptible wild animals or accompanied by vaccinated mother. Never allowed from third countries.
quarantine: None if requirements are met. Non-compliant pets can be returned to origin, isolated under official control at the owner's expense, or, as a last resort, euthanised.

Airport points of entry (2017 list): Bratislava, Košice, Piešťany, Poprad, Sliač, Žilina. Arrivals from another EU/EEA state: no veterinary border check, but documents must be carried. EU pet rules do not require pets to travel as cargo; cabin carriage is up to the operator. Non-compliance at a point of entry can lead to refusal, return or isolation at owner's cost.
